summary: Imagine a ring worn on an astronaut’s finger that can measure their physical and mental health. This portable, convenient device helps maintain the astronaut’s well-being for as long as possible; it features a smart display that shows the astronaut’s medical needs and automatically dispenses the appropriate medication from an onboard medicine kit.
details:
Our project consists of a smart ring connected to a display screen that monitors and presents the following health indicators:

  • Blood pressure
  • Blood glucose levels
  • Oxygen saturation (SpO₂)
  • Body temperature
  • Heart rate
  • Respiratory rate
  • Bone density
  • Radiation exposure
  • Muscle condition

The device operates using electricity. The screen detects any signs of physical stress or abnormalities in the astronaut’s body. Based on the readings, the system dispenses medication only when necessary, helping prevent unnecessary medication use and potential dependency.

A medication compartment located beneath the screen is preloaded before the mission with prescribed medications, which are dispensed when needed.

The purpose of our invention is based on one fundamental principle: illness may occur, but recovery should never be considered impossible. Regardless of how long an astronaut’s mission lasts, even if they become ill during the journey, our goal is to enable them to recover while still in space. Furthermore, early detection of certain changes may help astronauts prevent illnesses, physical deterioration, or neurological complications before they develop.

The device consists of three main components: a smart ring, a display screen, and a medication compartment. Further details about these components are available through the device’s 3D model link.

My team and I first considered the physical changes caused by the space environment, followed by their effects on the human body. The human body naturally responds to its surrounding environment. When physical environmental conditions change, the body experiences resistance and strong physiological and immune responses in an effort to protect itself.

We studied the physical changes in the space environment, measured their effects on the human body, and then explored pharmaceutical and medical solutions. We also investigated previous approaches that had failed, learned from their limitations, and used those lessons to develop new and innovative methods rather than repeating the same mistakes.

There are many additional details about our project that I would like to share. However, since the submission guidelines specify a maximum of seven slides, I have limited this explanation to the most essential information.
